Subject: Redline: Pricing Schedule & Waterfall Clawback (Order Form)

Jasmine —

Attached is Novus' redline of Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and the proposed language for the waterfall / clawback in the Order Form. High-level asks from legal and procurement: 

- Limit retrospective clawback window to 12 months (they've struck the 24-month language).
- Remove the automatic annual true-up mechanism unless Redwood agrees to an explicit stabilization band definition (they want clearer guardrails).
- Add a mutual cap on total post-termination reconciliation exposure (they propose 1.2x annual committed spend).

We flagged a few operational questions in the tracker (see sheet 2) — primarily around how KV-prefix caching credits would be included in usage calculations and whether burst capacity credits are excluded from clawback calculations.

Can you confirm Novus' non-negotiables so we can prepare a response? They're asking for a call tomorrow morning Pacific. Attachments: Pricing_Exhibit_B_redline_v1.pdf, redline_tracker_Novus.xlsx.

Thanks —
Elaine

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-10T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redline: Pricing Schedule & Waterfall Clawback (Order Form)

Team — forwarding Novus' redlines. Key operating asks below; Elaine asked for a call TOM. Please review and flag areas you want legal to push / accept. My initial read: solid ask on the 12-month cap; the remove-true-up ask is the risky one for us.

Suggested positions:
- 12-month retrospective cap: Acceptable from a commercial standpoint; keeps predictability for both sides.
- Remove annual true-up: Push back. Propose compromise: keep annual true-up but narrow scope and add a "Stabilization Band" definition (e.g., +/- 10% of committed tokens per quarter) so small variability doesn't trigger clawback.
- Mutual cap on post-termination reconciliation: We can discuss a lower multiplier (1.0x) or a tiered cap tied to committed volume.
- Clarify usage definition to exclude one-time onboarding credits and burst credits — operational ask to ensure clawback only hits billed usage.

Action items for call:
1) Ben — be prepared to explain how onboarding credits and burst credits are reflected in invoices and whether they are reversible.
2) Karthik — propose exact Stabilization Band wording and whether SLA credits offset clawback.
3) Marissa — commercial: think about offering a one-time onboarding credit to smooth acceptance (we can use that to soften the true-up retention).

I'll join the call and lead negotiation if we're aligned.

Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-10T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redline: Pricing Schedule & Waterfall Clawback (Order Form)

Agree with your read. My suggested negotiation language below — keep it tight.

1) 12-month retrospective: we accept Novus' 12-month window.

2) Annual true-up: counter-proposal — retain annual true-up but narrow triggers: only material deviation >15% aggregate from committed tokens for the 12-month period, and exclude one-time onboarding credits and burst credits from the usage basis. Add explicit language that SLA credits reduce clawback liabilities dollar-for-dollar.

3) Post-termination cap: propose 1.0x committed annual spend (their 1.2x is high for us). If they insist on higher, make it tiered: up to 1.0x for first 12 months, 1.2x if we discover systematic underreporting attributable to Redwood (we'll need audit rights).

4) Operational definitions: Accept only if we get an agreed definition of "Usage" (token vs invoice lines) and a documented mapping (we can provide a CSV export format).

5) Concessions: offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25k (applied to first invoice) in exchange for keeping the annual true-up with the narrowed triggers above.

If you're okay, I'll draft short amendment language for legal to review and bring into the call.

—Karthik

From: Elaine Hart <elaine.hart@novuscloud.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novuscloud.com
Date: 2027-08-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redline: Pricing Schedule & Waterfall Clawback (Order Form)

Jasmine —

Thanks for the quick internal turnaround. Novus is generally agreeable to the 12-month retrospective cap. Procurement pushed back on your proposed 1.0x post-termination cap; they're asking us to meet in the middle at 1.1x.

On the annual true-up: procurement will accept retention of an annual true-up only if the Stabilization Band is clearly defined. The band you proposed (±10%) is a good start, but their team prefers +/−12% for commercial seasonality. If Redwood is comfortable with a ±12% band and the explicit exclusion of onboarding and burst credits from the usage base, procurement will move forward.

We reviewed the $25k onboarding credit — procurement would like that to be documented as a one-time implementation credit applied within the first 60 days. If that's acceptable, we can push the amendment through legal.

I've uploaded our tracked redline and a short summary. If you're ready, I'll send a DocuSign amendment to lock these points.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-amendment
